recordingRights.basis: Official project policy states that volunteer recordings are dedicated to the public domain and may be reused, including commercially. It expressly confirms USA status and warns that copyright status may differ elsewhere.
recordingRights.boundary: Public availability, an Archive.org download button, and reader nationality are not used as licences. Recording dedication and underlying text edition are recorded separately. No universal all-jurisdiction legal clearance is claimed.

accentEvidence.use: Voluntary reader accent descriptions: Ruth Golding (reader 2607) describes RP/BBC English; Neeru Iyer (reader 3588) describes a South-Indian variety with qualification. The table explicitly warns that location is not necessarily accent; location cells are not used to infer variety.

Explicit labels attached to the same reader IDs: Kara Shallenberg 19, Southern California American; Annise 2544, Australian; Marianne Coleman-Hipkins 3928, Central North Island New Zealand. Different texts by those readers were selected; repeated North Wind and the Sun readings are not passed off as independent bodies.
accentEvidence.boundary: A source label describes the reader’s stated variety. It is not a new acoustic verification and does not certify that one reader represents every speaker in a region.

textRights.basis: Selected historical editions precede 1931 and are presented by LibriVox as USA public-domain texts. Edition titles, publication years, authors, named translators and known death dates are stored per source. Only the public-domain literary body is used, not modern introductions, illustrations or site design.
textRights.translationBoundary: Ancient Aesop alone does not clear a modern translation: the selected Vernon Jones 1912 English edition is identified, including the translator’s 1955 death. Verne’s selected English version identifies George Makepeace Towle. John Clare’s poem is transcribed from the historical 1831 edition cited by the source editor; that date is not asserted to be the first publication.
textRights.reuseChanges: Standard recording credits are retained in complete tracks and omitted from displayed body transcripts. Excerpts use contiguous complete sentences. Audio is re-encoded to mono 24 kHz MP3; no synthesis, speed or pitch change. Printed punctuation/capitalisation and necessary source-guided spelling are normalised and described.

authoring.questions: 48 project-original questions and Chinese explanations; no copyrighted examination question or answer copied.
authoring.asr: Actual local CPU int8 faster-whisper 1.2.1, base.en model, no supplied reference prompt. Model and original/selected audio hashes, actual recognised segments and a separate Fox/Crow tail pass are retained. ASR is fallible and was compared to print; it is not represented as a human auditory review.
authoring.dependencyBoundary: Optional authoring dependencies and model reside only in ignored work/. No Python/pip or ASR dependency is added to everyday learning or the native Node build.
authoring.verification: All eight selected bodies and 48 questions were checked clause by clause against print and actual ASR evidence by Codex. Real ffmpeg decoding, non-silence, MP3 format, duration and raw byte hashes are audited separately.
authoring.limits: Historical literary readings rather than spontaneous contemporary conversation. A2/B1/B2 are target levels, not learner-calibrated difficulty. Human-source identity does not establish pronunciation scoring reliability, accent certification or IELTS performance.

rebuild: Normal offline release: node tools/build-curriculum.cjs; node tools/audit-human-listening.cjs --decode. Checked-in prepared audio and metadata are sufficient; no external service is needed.

Optional author re-import: install faster-whisper 1.2.1 only into work/human-asr-python using a separately installed Python; provide ffmpeg/ffprobe on the authoring PATH. Run node tools/import-human-listening.cjs --prepare-asr; python tools/transcribe-human-listening.py; node tools/import-human-listening.cjs; node tools/build-curriculum.cjs; node tools/audit-human-listening.cjs --decode.

Import reuses a locally present original MP3. Delete an individual course-asset cache only if deliberately re-fetching a changed public original; never modify learner data. The importer stores original and selected hashes so a changed upstream file remains detectable.
